identity.libraryClass: custom numpy transition-count MLE (no canonical sklearn-family class; cf. pomegranate.MarkovChain)
identity.description: First-order Markov chain over OBSERVED discrete states: estimates the K x K transition-probability matrix by counting state-to-state transitions across sequences. The matrix IS the model — fully inspectable, fit by counting, no latent structure.

consumes.note: per-entity ordered sequences of discrete state tokens (e.g. monthly engagement tier); unsupervised — no target
an upstream decoder's state path (e.g. HMM Viterbi output) is itself a legal observed-state input — the chain-on-decoded-states composition

emits.note: the row-stochastic K x K matrix — the model's entire fitted knowledge, directly consumable downstream (steady-state analysis, churn-path features)
per-sequence log-likelihood under the fitted chain — 'how typical is this member's path' as a downstream feature or anomaly-ish signal

laplace_alpha.note: additive smoothing pseudo-count — the only real knob; keeps unobserved transitions from annihilating held-out likelihood

min_state_support.note: states with fewer total observations than this are pooled into a rare-state bucket before counting

unk_state.note: reserve an explicit UNK row/column so unseen states at scoring time remain scoreable

invariances.why: inputs are categorical state tokens — there is no numeric scale anywhere in the fit
any bijective recoding of the state alphabet yields an isomorphic transition matrix; only the labels move
a missing state token breaks adjacency — splicing over a gap fabricates a transition that never happened; gaps must be segmented or given an explicit missing-state token
the state alphabet IS categorical; counting operates on tokens directly, no encoding step
assumes the first-order Markov property (next state depends only on current) and time-homogeneous transition probabilities
counting is sample-efficient for small alphabets, but the K^2 cells each need support — large K with few sequences leaves the matrix sparse and smoothing-dependent
a state never seen in training has no row or column — the model is undefined outside the observed alphabet (hence the UNK-state hedge)

featureStats.why: the matrix has K^2 cells to support with transition counts; a large alphabet against a small corpus flags pooling or a coarser state definition
an unobserved (i,j) cell gets probability zero and annihilates the likelihood of any future sequence containing that transition — the Laplace-smoothing trigger
a length-L sequence contributes L-1 transitions; a corpus of length-1 sequences carries zero transition information

modelMetrics.why: perplexity on held-out sequences is the honest scoreboard for a generative sequence model — training-set transition recall proves nothing
a significant LR for a second-order chain over first-order says the memorylessness assumption is violated — the gate toward higher order or an HMM

edgeCases.condition: unseen state token at scoring time
transition behavior drifts over calendar time
edgeCases.behavior: the single matrix is a blur of regimes
edgeCases.note: markov_switching / hmm are the regime-aware siblings

driver.wrapperNeeds: sequence adapter: (entity_id, order_col, state_col) -> per-entity ordered token lists, segmented at gaps; score maps to per-sequence log-likelihood
driver.threadSafety: stateless counting; fit and score are thread-safe

canBeSeeds.via: score -> features:tabular adapter (per-entity path log-likelihood as a model feature)

placementClaims.why: a gap spliced over creates a spurious transition; sequences must be segmented at gaps or carry an explicit missing-state token before counting
bijective recoding of tokens is a no-op on the fit; there is no numeric transform to apply
categorical states carry no scale — nothing to standardize
native-categorical: counting consumes tokens directly; integer coding is an internal implementation detail, not a pipeline stage
